status_summary: DHS did the opposite on the cap: a joint DHS and Labor rule published 2026-02-03 (effective 2026-01-30 through 2026-09-30) made up to 64,716 additional H-2B visas available for FY2026 to employers attesting to irreparable harm, using authority that Congress extended in the continuing appropriations act signed 2025-11-12 (Public Law 119-37). A similar rule for FY2025 had been published on 2024-12-02, before the period covered, and a Labor notice of 2026-07-30 submitting the FY2026 attestation form for OMB review shows the process continuing. On the country list, a DHS final rule of 2024-12-18, effective 2025-01-17, removed the requirement that H-2 petitions be limited to nationals of listed countries; no later rule supporting the list was found.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-37, a continuing appropriations act, extended the discretionary H-2B supplemental visa authority into FY2026.
DHS and Labor published a rule releasing up to 64,716 additional H-2B visas for FY2026 in three allocations by start date, for employers attesting to irreparable harm.
Labor submitted for OMB review the attestation form for H-2B employers under the supplemental authority as extended by Public Law 119-37.

title: Stop raising the H-2B cap by discretion and issue no H-2 eligible-country rules
uncertainties: Whether the H-2 Modernization rule was delayed or changed after January 2025, and whether DHS has since published any annual country-list notice, was not confirmed beyond a Federal Register search returning none after November 2024. The FY2026 rule as read shows no countries reserved, unlike the FY2025 rule, but its last part was not read. Whether a supplemental H-2B authority applies to FY2027 was not found. H-2A and other guest worker questions, and the related cap-and-phase-down recommendation in the labor chapter, are in c18-07. Stage diverged reflects the cap element; the country-list element matches the recommendation only in that no supporting rule was issued after the list was removed by a rule that predates the period.
